tEn: Brett on Beating China, Racing Tesla, and the Humanoid Timeline
tZh: Brett 谈击败中国、与特斯拉竞速及人形机器人时间表
sEn: Brett breaks down the humanoid race with China and Tesla, the four stages of robot development, and why Figure 4 could be the iPhone moment for robots.
sZh: Brett 解析与中美的机器人竞赛、机器人发展的四个阶段，以及为何 Figure 4 可能成为机器人的 iPhone 时刻。

consensus.en: Humanoid robotics has four stages: functional hardware, AI recipe, scaling intelligence, then scaling robots.
consensus.zh: 人形机器人分四个阶段：可用硬件、AI 配方、Scaling（规模扩张）智能，再到 Scaling（规模扩张）机器人。

consensus.en: The core bottleneck for home robots is intelligence, not hardware or integration.
consensus.zh: 家用机器人的核心瓶颈是智能，而非硬件或集成。

consensus.en: Figure 2.5 showed the first humanoid scaling laws: more data yields log-linear gains.
consensus.zh: Figure 2.5 首次展示人形机器人的缩放定律：数据越多，收益呈对数线性增长。

consensus.en: All inference runs onboard; cloud is only for speech and fleet agent orchestration.
consensus.zh: 所有推理都在机器人本体运行，云端只负责语音和机群智能体编排。

consensus.en: Figure will only ship a home robot when it is an Apple-quality magical product.
consensus.zh: Figure 只在产品达到苹果级品质、体验惊艳时才把家用机器人推向市场。

consensus.en: Robotics is necessary to avoid a dystopian future where digital ASI bosses humans around.
consensus.zh: 机器人是避免数字超级智能驱使人类这一反乌托邦未来的必要条件。

contrarian.en: China's dancing robots are open-loop RL replays, orthogonal to real general robotics.
contrarian.zh: 中国的跳舞机器人是开环强化学习回放，与真正的通用机器人技术正交。

contrarian.en: Tesla is not a real competitor; the race is against the collective of China.
contrarian.zh: 特斯拉并非真正对手，这场竞赛的对手是中国的集体力量。

contrarian.en: Language and multimodal models operating robots are not real robotics models.
contrarian.zh: 让语言和多模态模型操控机器人，算不上真正的机器人模型。

contrarian.en: Googly eyes on robots are a con that misrepresents what the technology can do.
contrarian.zh: 给机器人装卡通眼睛是一种欺骗，歪曲了这项技术的真实能力。

contrarian.en: Vertical integration is mandatory: off-the-shelf actuators were three times too big and costly.
contrarian.zh: 垂直整合是必须的：现成执行器体积和成本都超标三倍。

contrarian.en: Persistent personality should live in the cloud, not on the device, and port across robots.
contrarian.zh: 持久人格应存于云端而非设备，并可在不同机器人间迁移。

turns.en: As you think about competition, is it Tesla and China? Is that the way you see it in the world right now?
turns.zh: 当你考虑竞争时，是特斯拉和中国吗？你现在是这样看世界的吗？

turns.en: I personally haven't seen it much at a Tesla in two or three years. I've seen China do a lot of dancing. We care about something very different than what we think China cares about. We just got to go beat them. It's a real race here. The work isn't really practical. The technology stack needed to get there isn't practical. And the AI stack to do it can be done by a senior in college. My view is there's roughly four stages for this humanoid race. Chapter one of this book is you have to build really good functional hardware. Two is you have to be able to build an AI recipe. Chapter three and four for me are scaling intelligence and scaling robots.
turns.zh: 我个人已经两三年没怎么在特斯拉看到它了。我看到中国做了很多跳舞。我们关心的事情和我们认为中国关心的事情非常不同。我们就是要打败他们。这是一场真正的竞赛。这项工作并不实际。达到那里所需的技术栈并不实际。而实现它的 AI 栈，一个大学生就能做。我的观点是，这场人形机器人竞赛大致有四个阶段。这本书的第一章是你必须构建真正好的功能性硬件。第二是你必须能够构建 AI 配方。对我来说，第三和第四章是扩展智能和扩展机器人。

turns.en: What might we see with Figure 4? What areas are you focusing on making improvements?
turns.zh: Figure 4 可能会让我们看到什么？你们专注于在哪些领域进行改进？

turns.en: We're like in the flip phone era for humanoids. Figure 4 is probably the iPhone 1 moment we're going to have here soon. We need the robot to get cheaper. We're trying to make the robot more capable. A little sneak peek of that is we've been working on the hands. A Figure 4 with a glove and a human with a glove is almost indistinguishable.
turns.zh: 对于人形机器人，我们就像处于翻盖手机时代。Figure 4 可能就是我们即将迎来的 iPhone 1 时刻。我们需要让机器人更便宜。我们正努力让机器人更强大。稍微透露一点，我们一直在研究手部。戴手套的 Figure 4 和戴手套的人类几乎无法区分。

turns.en: That's like an iPhone moment.
turns.zh: 那就像 iPhone 时刻。

turns.en: Figure 3 is probably the best humanoid on the market by far, but it'll make Figure 3 look like a caveman.
turns.zh: Figure 3 可能是目前市场上最好的的人形机器人，但它会让 Figure 3 看起来像穴居人。

turns.en: Now that's a moon shot, ladies and gentlemen. This episode is brought to you by the Abundance Summit and Link Ventures. So Brett, good to be here for our annual catch up. It's been about a year since David and I were here to see Figure and quite the difference to walk in. You just parked in the parking lot over there and walk in and there's like 100 robots outside to greet you. So my question is what do you call a group of robots? Like I'm calling a flock of Figures. Do you have a name for them?
turns.zh: 女士们先生们，那是一个登月计划。本集由 Abundance Summit 和 Link Ventures 赞助。Brett，很高兴来这里进行我们的年度交流。距离 David 和我来这里看 Figure 已经大约一年了，走进来的感觉大不相同。你刚把车停在那边停车场，走进来，外面就有大约 100 个机器人迎接你。所以我的问题是，你怎么称呼一群机器人？我称之为一群 Figure。你们有名字吗？

turns.en: Yeah. Those are our visitor bots. They walk around all of campus. They can open doors, walk on any stairs, use the elevators. And they're there to greet people, talk. And then we're right now working on trying to get them to like, you know, do like get coffee for folks.
turns.zh: 是的。那些是我们的访客机器人。它们在整个园区里走动。它们能开门、走任何楼梯、使用电梯。它们在那里迎接人们、交谈。然后我们现在正努力让它们像，你知道，为人们拿咖啡。

turns.en: Nice.
turns.zh: 不错。

turns.en: We have kind of a stretch goal of like it'd be great if you can come to campus and never talk to a human as you get set up. I um you know, like get fully checked in, walk to the conference room, do a like go to the bathroom, like all done through a humanoid.
turns.zh: 我们有一个延伸目标，比如如果你能来园区，在办理手续时从不和人类交谈，那就太好了。我，嗯，你知道，比如完全登记入住，走到会议室，去洗手间，所有这些都通过人形机器人完成。

turns.en: Let me show you where I was built. Let me show you what I'm doing all day.
turns.zh: 让我展示给你看我是在哪里被建造的。让我展示给你看我整天在做什么。

turns.en: Exactly. Like we do that all the time. So like why not? We should have a humanoid do it.
turns.zh: 没错。就像我们一直这样做。所以为什么不呢？我们应该让人形机器人来做。

turns.en: And you said something a minute ago that's pretty profound. You have more Figure robots than humans now.
turns.zh: 你一分钟前说了一些很深刻的话。你现在拥有的 Figure 机器人比人类还多。

turns.en: Yeah, we have more Figure robots on campus than humans.
turns.zh: 是的，我们园区里的 Figure 机器人比人类多。

turns.en: When did that happen?
turns.zh: 那是什么时候发生的？

turns.en: Probably like four or five months ago we crossed the number. I think we have like seven, eight hundred people here. So we crossed the number of, yeah, we have more robots now. We have many more now than humans.
turns.zh: 大概四五个月前我们超过了这个数字。我想我们这里大约有七八百人。所以我们超过了这个数字，是的，我们现在有更多机器人。我们现在比人类多得多。

turns.en: And you're up to how many produced at this point?
turns.zh: 你们现在生产了多少？

turns.en: I don't know. Like 1,500 or so on campus, something like that. An order of like we have well over a thousand on campus and we have robots out in other places in the world as well.
turns.zh: 我不知道。园区里大概有 1500 个左右，差不多这样。数量级上，我们园区里有一千多个，我们在世界其他地方也有机器人。

turns.en: Oh, nice. So we're seeing Figure 3 around here. Last time we were here, you were just transitioning to Figure 3, I think at that point. How long before I'm talking to the Figure?
turns.zh: 哦，不错。所以我们在这里看到的是 Figure 3。上次我们来的时候，我想你当时刚刚过渡到 Figure 3。还要多久我才能和 Figure 对话？

turns.en: You can talk to any robot here.
turns.zh: 你可以和这里的任何机器人交谈。

turns.en: Yeah?
turns.zh: 是吗？

turns.en: Yeah, you can stop it and just ask a question. You can talk to it. It's got real-time speech to speech. Yeah. So every robot here is equipped with speaker and mic. We actually use HARQ for our voice AI. And every robot here has got full real-time speech to speech.
turns.zh: 是的，你可以让它停下来，直接问问题。你可以和它交谈。它有实时语音到语音。是的。所以这里的每个机器人都配备了扬声器和麦克风。我们实际上使用 HARQ 作为我们的语音 AI。这里的每个机器人都有完整的实时语音到语音。

turns.en: Incredible.
turns.zh: 不可思议。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Incredible. So a lot of people are asking me, so when am I going to be able to get my... Let's jump into some timelines and applications to kick things off because I think that's the most interesting. When can I order a Figure for the home? I think most people want to know that question.
turns.zh: 不可思议。所以很多人问我，我什么时候能拿到我的……让我们先谈谈时间线和应用，因为我觉得那是最有趣的。我什么时候可以订购家用 Figure？我想大多数人都想知道这个问题。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean at a high level we have two tracks. We want to ship robots commercially and we want to ship robots in the home. They're really different spaces. The commercial markets in some way easier where it's like you know very well-specified tasks. You can almost like write down a piece of paper exactly what the robot's doing every day. It doesn't really deviate from it. But it's really hard in the sense of like we have a lot of speed and performance goals to go hit and we mess up you get fired. No great. Not great. So really tough. On the home it's a little bit of opposite. We don't need to do it at the speeds we would need on the commercial market, but then there's not really a specified task. Every home is different. I bet if we ask like what kind of appliances three of us have, they're all different in all of our homes. The setups the home different in the homes. The things we'll want the robot to do be like you know we'll change quite dynamically. So we're working on both in parallel. We think they're both an intelligence problem really. Like how do we get like the robot to I mean the robot Figure 3 is really capable of doing most things in a home. So we're working really hard on trying to build like larger pre-trained models and doing a lot more work in post-training in RL to really really try to crack this problem. What are we going to have in the homes? Like Figure like so I think you'll get a little bit different of opinion if you talk to other maybe companies in the space, but like our view here is that Figure will ship a robot when it ships like a really high quality product in the home. Like it needs to be able to walk into the home, talk to you, be able to do real work. Like we don't want to be teleoperating the home. We don't want the robot to be having any issues and failures or stopping because the robot's unsure what to do. The robot needs like be like a high quality product when it enters the home. Like an Apple style quality product when it enters the home.
turns.zh: 是的。我的意思是，在高层次上我们有两条轨道。我们想商业出货机器人，也想在家庭中出货机器人。它们是非常不同的空间。商业市场在某种程度上更容易，因为任务非常明确。你几乎可以在一张纸上写下机器人每天确切在做什么。它不会偏离。但真的很难，因为我们要达到很多速度和性能目标，如果我们搞砸了，你就会被解雇。不太好。不太好。所以真的很难。在家庭方面有点相反。我们不需要以商业市场所需的速度来做，但也没有真正指定的任务。每个家庭都不同。我敢打赌，如果我们问我们三个人有什么电器，我们所有家庭都不同。家庭的设置不同。我们希望机器人做的事情会动态变化。所以我们并行推进两者。我们认为它们实际上都是智能问题。比如我们如何让机器人——我的意思是 Figure 3 真的有能力做家庭中的大多数事情。所以我们正在努力构建更大的预训练模型，并在后训练和强化学习方面做更多工作，真正尝试解决这个问题。我们将在家庭中拥有什么？像 Figure——所以我认为如果你和这个领域的其他公司交谈，你会得到稍微不同的意见，但我们这里的观点是，Figure 将在家庭中出货真正高质量的产品时才会出货机器人。它需要能够走进家庭，与你交谈，能够做真正的工作。我们不想远程操作家庭。我们不希望机器人出现任何问题、故障或因为不确定该做什么而停下来。机器人进入家庭时需要像高质量产品。像苹果风格的高质量产品进入家庭。

turns.en: Kids and the dog to worry about too.
turns.zh: 还要担心孩子和狗。

turns.en: Exactly, but it needs to work. Like it needs to be able to go in there and be like this magical experience of having like another person in the home. So that's our launch criteria. We're not going to launch before then. I think you'll see others do that and it will just like in my mind won't work.
turns.zh: 没错，但它需要能工作。它需要能够进入那里，就像家里有另一个人一样的奇妙体验。所以那是我们的发布标准。我们不会在那之前发布。我想你会看到其他人这样做，但在我看来那行不通。

turns.en: It'll be like what you've seen with AI devices. You've seen this now with Humane and Rabbit and these other groups in the AI device space. It just isn't going to work until you have a really magical product. So for us, we're trying to crack that. The key constraint here is intelligence. The Figure 3 robots have the ability to fold laundry, do dishes, unload groceries, open the refrigerator, open the oven, do real work in the home, like clean the house up. We've shown some of that, but we need to be able to do that end to end for a dozen plus hours per day, every single day, seven days a week, for years.
turns.zh: 就像你们看到的 AI 设备。你们已经看到 Humane 和 Rabbit 以及 AI 设备领域的其他团队。除非你有真正神奇的产品，否则它就是行不通。所以对我们来说，我们正试图攻克这一点。这里的关键约束是智能。Figure 3 机器人有能力叠衣服、洗碗、卸货、打开冰箱、打开烤箱，在家里做真正的工作，比如打扫房子。我们已经展示了其中一些，但我们需要能够端到端地做到这一点，每天十几个小时，每天如此，每周七天，持续多年。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So we're pushing on that. I would say the biggest constraint is an intelligence constraint. How do you drop a robot into any home we would pick? Just talking to it, have it do useful work. There are other things. There's an integration problem, there's a safety problem, there's other things that are really hard. But by and large it's an intelligence problem we're trying to crack.
turns.zh: 所以我们正在推进这一点。我想说最大的约束是智能约束。你如何把机器人放到我们选择的任何家庭中？只需与它交谈，让它做有用的工作。还有其他事情。有集成问题，有安全问题，还有其他非常困难的事情。但总的来说，这是一个我们试图攻克的智能问题。

turns.en: But again, without a promise and I won't tell anybody, 27, 28?
turns.zh: 但再说一次，不作承诺，我也不会告诉任何人，27、28 年？

turns.en: I mean we're doing testing now and we'll be in anywhere from 20 to new net new homes we haven't been in in California doing testing as of right now.
turns.zh: 我的意思是我们现在正在进行测试，我们将在加利福尼亚州进入 20 到全新未涉足的家庭进行测试，截至目前。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: And we've been doing this since the launch of Helix 2.5. So we're doing that mostly for evaluations and evals for our models and a ton of hardcore testing. My forecast: I think the first thing we really need is we need to prove to ourselves is we can do end-to-end work in a zero-shot environment, meaning a home we've never been in. We haven't trained in it, we haven't seen any objects before. Just through speech we can take commands, like say a prompt, and we can basically do end-to-end work. We're doing that really well today on the micro level. Like if you ask it to do one thing like make the bed or say unload dishes from the dishwasher.
turns.zh: 自 Helix 2.5 发布以来我们一直在这样做。所以我们这样做主要是为了评估和我们的模型评估，以及大量硬核测试。我的预测：我认为我们真正需要的第一件事是向自己证明，我们可以在零样本环境中完成端到端工作，即我们从未去过的家庭。我们没有在其中训练过，我们以前没有见过任何物体。只需通过语音，我们可以接受命令，比如给出一个提示，我们基本上可以完成端到端工作。我们今天在微观层面上做得非常好。比如如果你让它做一件事，比如铺床或者说从洗碗机里卸碗。

turns.en: Just did that actually. Totally open-ended prompt. No preconceived what I'm going to ask you to do.
turns.zh: 实际上刚做了那个。完全开放式的提示。没有预先设想我要让你做什么。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And it takes a really good shot at any task right out of pure prompt.
turns.zh: 它仅凭纯提示就能对任何任务做出很好的尝试。

turns.en: Yeah. So okay maybe like sorry a little robust, but we need to be able to go off and do that fully end-to-end now over long horizons. We're training now larger and larger models. What you saw there in Black Box today was Helix 3. It was probably the only people in the world that have seen this outside this office. And for me, I don't know what you guys were feeling, but it feels for me like a really baby AGI moment. I'd characterize it like it's like an adult body, like adult—it's a robot, but adult human, like a really dumb adult human. Like a two-year-old in an adult body. And you can basically ask it whatever you want and it can do a lot of things and some things it just can't do well at, but it was significantly undertrained. It was our first model checkpoint coming out of Helix 3. We now have much larger models that are being trained that we're evaluating even this week. So my bet is—you ask like what date.
turns.zh: 是的。所以好吧，也许有点啰嗦，但我们需要能够现在在长视野上完全端到端地做到这一点。我们现在正在训练越来越大的模型。你们今天在 Black Box 看到的那个是 Helix 3。这可能是世界上除了这个办公室之外唯一看过它的人。对我来说，我不知道你们感觉如何，但对我来说，这感觉像是一个真正的婴儿 AGI 时刻。我把它描述为像一个成年人的身体，像一个成年人——它是一个机器人，但像成年人，像一个非常笨的成年人。像一个两岁小孩在成年人的身体里。你基本上可以问它任何你想要的东西，它可以做很多事情，有些事情它就是不擅长，但它训练得严重不足。这是我们 Helix 3 的第一个模型检查点。我们现在有更大的模型正在训练中，我们甚至这周就在评估。所以我的赌注是——你问像什么日期。

turns.en: What year?
turns.zh: 哪一年？

turns.en: My bet is within the next—I hope to see, I obviously can't promise, but I hope to see in the next sub six months, perhaps even sooner, we can put a robot into any home and do fairly large long-horizon tasks end to end.
turns.zh: 我的赌注是在接下来的——我希望看到，我显然不能承诺，但我希望在接下来的六个月内，甚至更早，我们可以把机器人放进任何家庭，并端到端地完成相当大的长视野任务。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Like over hours and hours.
turns.zh: 比如持续数小时。

turns.en: And then the question of when you would actually sell them to consumers.
turns.zh: 然后是你什么时候真正向消费者出售它们的问题。

turns.en: Yeah, then we got to figure out how to get them to consumers, make sure they're really safe. The reliability is really high. There's no issues and faults.
turns.zh: 是的，然后我们必须弄清楚如何将它们送到消费者手中，确保它们非常安全。可靠性非常高。没有问题和故障。

turns.en: Do you think you're going to keep robot maintenance and repair as a Figure in-house capability or are you going to approve outside vendors to do that all over the world?
turns.zh: 你认为你会将机器人维护和修理保留为 Figure 的内部能力，还是会批准外部供应商在世界各地进行这项工作？

turns.en: For now we're going to do it ourselves.
turns.zh: 目前我们将自己来做。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: We really want to make sure the robot is the highest quality experience in the home. And we know the robot better than anybody else and we built them, so we're going to do that ourselves.
turns.zh: 我们真的想确保机器人在家中提供最高质量的体验。我们比任何人都更了解机器人，而且是我们建造的，所以我们将自己来做。

turns.en: Can just crawl into a box and ship itself back.
turns.zh: 它可以爬进一个盒子然后把自己寄回来。

turns.en: Yep, totally. There's like many ways to solve this problem. The end state is for sure us not doing everything. But in the beginning as we ramp the product up, you really want this incredible experience in the home. It's basically just like another human is in your house helping you out. turns.zh: 我觉得他在做——我猜他是在做 AI 设备相关的工作。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um, I don't know if he's working on an iPhone killer, but now they got afraid of saying that, but it's some device that has AI embedded in it that's so compelling. But your point about there being a centerpiece—your personal information isn't going to be everywhere. You're only going to trust a limited number of centerpieces. And so I think they want that device to be the centerpiece, not the iPhone. You obviously have the same vision with Hark.
turns.zh: 嗯，我不知道他是不是在做 iPhone 杀手，但现在他们不敢这么说了，但那是某种嵌入了 AI 的设备，非常引人注目。但你说的关于有一个中心设备的观点——你的个人信息不会到处都是。你只会信任有限数量的中心设备。所以我认为他们希望那个设备成为中心，而不是 iPhone。你显然对 Hark 有同样的愿景。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So I can see how those are going to play out.
turns.zh: 所以我能看到这些将如何发展。

turns.en: Not going to be the iPhone. Like it's—the iPhone is going to go away. Like—
turns.zh: 不会是 iPhone。就像——iPhone 会消失。就像——

turns.en: All right, we're calling it here: the decline of Apple.
turns.zh: 好吧，我们就在这里宣布：苹果的衰落。

turns.en: I mean, like, let's just call it. And you listen—if you take the extreme case, in 10 years we're not using a traditional phone.
turns.zh: 我是说，我们就这么说吧。你听着——如果你考虑极端情况，10 年后我们不会使用传统手机。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: You know what I mean? Like I just like—so we know that like—
turns.zh: 你懂我的意思吗？就像我只是——所以我们知道就像——

turns.en: It's like—it's like Turnus really has a challenge right now because they've been gliding forever on the iPhone and it's going to get challenged from a dozen different places.
turns.zh: 就像——就像 Turnus 现在真的面临挑战，因为他们一直靠 iPhone 滑行，而它将受到来自十几个不同地方的挑战。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Man, I've had this thing where I've thought I'd wake up at some point every day and see Tim Cook or whatever John get on some emergency PR event and basically say, 'Hey, we bought $100 billion of GPUs. We're bringing the top team in the world. We're going to go up pre-training hard. In the meantime, we're going to use other models, and this is going to be so core to the experience interface with consumers long term that we really need to own it, understand it, and embed it.' And it's been crazy to see nothing. And it's now across the point, probably about a year ago, to a point where it's really too hard to turn around.
turns.zh: 老兄，我一直有这种想法，我原以为每天某个时候醒来会看到 Tim Cook 或 John 参加某种紧急公关活动，基本上说：‘嘿，我们买了 1000 亿美元的 GPU。我们带来了世界顶级团队。我们要大力推进预训练。与此同时，我们将使用其他模型，从长远来看，这对与消费者的体验界面如此核心，我们真的需要拥有它、理解它并嵌入它。’而令人疯狂的是，什么都没发生。现在已经过了那个点，大概一年前，到了一个真的很难扭转的地步。

turns.en: You think?
turns.zh: 你觉得？

turns.en: It's for sure. It's like there's—
turns.zh: 这是肯定的。就像有——

turns.en: Lost so much momentum.
turns.zh: 失去了太多势头。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: You want to co-design the hardware and the models together. You really want to think about these AI devices as just a pure interface. It could be BCI in the brain, it could be language devices that we're working through now. Like this is just the interface to this raw intelligence in there inside that's going to be human-like just for you. And they need to be co-designed together.
turns.zh: 你想共同设计硬件和模型。你真的想把这些 AI 设备看作纯粹的界面。它可能是大脑中的 BCI，也可能是我们现在正在研究的语言设备。就像这只是内部原始智能的界面，那将为你而变得像人一样。它们需要一起共同设计。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And it's not something you just flop in. And so instead of like—
turns.zh: 这不是你随便就能搞定的。所以与其像——

turns.en: In BCI?
turns.zh: 在 BCI 方面？

turns.en: Yeah. I think I'm very interested in BCI. I think it's one of the most—I think it's a very important vector to be on for AI interfacing long term. I just—
turns.zh: 是的。我认为我对 BCI 非常感兴趣。我认为它是最——我认为从长远来看，它是 AI 接口的一个非常重要的方向。我只是——

turns.en: I'm invested in four of the companies right now and I've just seen some—I just had some meetings yesterday. It's blowing my mind. We're on the precipice of being able to actually get to a mouse connectome.
turns.zh: 我现在投资了四家公司，我刚刚看到一些——我昨天刚开了一些会。这让我大开眼界。我们正处于能够真正获得小鼠连接组的边缘。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And then a human connectome.
turns.zh: 然后是人类连接组。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And then the world changes.
turns.zh: 然后世界就变了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: That's sick. We should debrief at some point. Like I think—
turns.zh: 太棒了。我们以后应该详细聊聊。就像我觉得——

turns.en: I would love to make some introductions. There's some amazing company.
turns.zh: 我很乐意做一些介绍。有一些很棒的公司。

turns.en: Yeah. I think we're going to this phase of like kind of beyond where we're at now is like language device phase. I think there's a phase kind of after that of like BCI and alignment into the brain. I think it's going to be really important. I expect Heart to be working through that whole process all the way through. So I think we're like—but certainly right now there's like an upgrade cycle coming for traditional computers and phones. And what I can tell you by just using some of the products here internally is it's going to be phenomenal. It's going to be a much better experience.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为我们正在进入这个阶段，超越我们现在所处的语言设备阶段。我认为之后会有一个 BCI 和将对齐技术融入大脑的阶段。我认为这将非常重要。我期望 Heart 会全程参与整个过程。所以我认为我们就像——但当然现在传统电脑和手机即将迎来升级周期。我只能告诉你，仅通过内部使用一些产品，它将是惊人的。它将带来更好的体验。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯是的。

turns.en: Because we haven't changed in 20 years.
turns.zh: 因为我们 20 年没变了。

turns.en: It's literally 20 years and now we're just plopping AI into it and it's kind of like the interfaces are just really reactionary. Like you have to kind of control the phone yourself, but we've—man, we built this thing that can think now and use computers and it can speak to you and it can see and it can build persistent almost perfect memory. And you know, you want to be able to interface with that in real time. And even, you know, have it with you everywhere you go. And we don't have anything near like that in the world today, but we will shortly.
turns.zh: literally 20 年了，现在我们只是把 AI 塞进去，这有点像界面真的非常被动。就像你必须自己控制手机，但我们——老兄，我们造出了这个东西，它现在能思考、能使用电脑、能和你说话、能看，还能建立持久几乎完美的记忆。你知道，你希望能够实时与它交互。甚至，你知道，让它伴随你到任何地方。今天世界上还没有任何接近这样的东西，但我们很快就会有了。

turns.en: It's coming.
turns.zh: 它要来了。

turns.en: Yeah. Well, after AI is the interface, you basically use the phone as a camera, but the cameras are like three bucks.
turns.zh: 是的。好吧，在 AI 成为界面之后，你基本上把手机当作相机，但相机大概只要三美元。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It's like, okay, what—why did I pay 1,500 bucks? I got a $3 camera.
turns.zh: 就像，好吧，什么——我为什么花了 1500 美元？我得到了一个 3 美元的相机。

turns.en: I mean, phones are incredible. It's just like there is just like a next leg upcoming. It's going to be great.
turns.zh: 我是说，手机很不可思议。只是就像即将迎来下一段。它会很棒。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It's about time.
turns.zh: 是时候了。

turns.en: Hey, let's wrap with the conversation on regulation because I am curious what you're thinking here. We've got Bernie Sanders and AOC saying, you know, we got to stop, slow down, prevent RSI. And I have to imagine—I don't know if you're in those conversations at all, but I have to imagine there's going to be a similar kind of like slow down. We don't need robots on our streets. It's not safe for the citizenry. How do you think about that? Are you having those conversations and is there any—you know, is there real concern that the public should have in this regard?
turns.zh: 嘿，让我们以监管的讨论来收尾，因为我很好奇你在这里的想法。我们有伯尼·桑德斯和 AOC 说，你知道，我们必须停止、放缓、防止 RSI。而我不得不想象——我不知道你是否参与那些对话，但我不得不想象会有类似的放缓。我们不需要机器人在我们的街道上。这对公民不安全。你如何看待这一点？你在进行那些对话吗？有没有——你知道，公众在这方面应该有真正的担忧吗？

turns.en: I can speak for our plans. Our plans are to launch a really high-quality product that works really well into the market.
turns.zh: 我可以代表我们的计划。我们的计划是推出一款真正高质量的产品，它能很好地进入市场。

turns.en: And safe.
turns.zh: 而且安全。

turns.en: And safe. Like we don't want to be out there like, you know, telly up in the robot around and doing unsafe work, shipping too early. So we're making incremental steps now. We shipped first commercially last year. We're shipping even more this year.
turns.zh: 而且安全。就像我们不想像，你知道，在机器人上电视到处跑，做不安全的工作，过早发货。所以我们现在正在采取渐进步骤。我们去年首次商业发货。今年我们会发货更多。

turns.en: Have you seen any inkling from regulators to start speaking about humanoid robotics the same way they're speaking about superintelligence?
turns.zh: 你看到监管机构有任何迹象开始像谈论超级智能那样谈论类人机器人吗？

turns.en: We really haven't seen that like public facing. We've even rumblings of this. We've seen like there's been like, you know, the only thing we've been aware of the last like 90 days is the FCC ban on humanoid on Chinese humanoids. Um beyond that, we haven't seen anything, you know, come across our desk. I think um, we're you know, to also a little bit personal to Like I don't fly to DC every week and try to get my nose in this. Like I really want to be here. I'm here.
turns.zh: 我们真的没有看到那种面向公众的。我们甚至有一些传言。我们看到就像，你知道，过去 90 天我们唯一意识到的是 FCC 对中国类人机器人的禁令。嗯，除此之外，我们还没有看到任何东西，你知道，出现在我们桌上。我认为嗯，我们你知道，也有点个人来说，就像我不会每周飞往华盛顿特区试图插手这件事。就像我真的想在这里。我在这里。

turns.en: I'm here trying to build and I want to build awesome robots regardless. There are going to be robots coming. They're going to be great for the world. I think the same with AI. It's going to be great. If humanity woke up one day and just didn't want AI, we can just shut down the internet. We can just close it. But we don't want that. It's going to be really helpful for the whole entire world. And there will be like whatever, Bernie Sanders the world or whatever here, but for us, we're just really focused on the mission of trying to build and ship your robots. And we're here every day trying to go do that.
turns.zh: 我来这里是为了打造机器人，无论如何我都想打造出很棒的机器人。机器人即将到来，它们会对世界大有裨益。我认为 AI 也是如此，它会非常棒。如果有一天人类醒来突然不想要 AI 了，我们可以直接关掉互联网，直接关闭它。但我们不想那样。它会对全世界非常有帮助。会有像伯尼·桑德斯那样的人或别的什么，但对我们来说，我们只是非常专注于打造和交付机器人的使命。我们每天都在为此努力。

turns.en: I got a question just to inspire all the entrepreneurs out there. So, you know, I grew up a big Steve Jobs fan too and I think a lot about how much more he could have done in his life, but in that era you could only do one thing at a time and nobody had super voting control and all that and then when Google came along and then Zuckerberg came along, it switched to this era where the founders control the companies
turns.zh: 我有个问题，想激励一下所有的创业者。你知道，我也是个史蒂夫·乔布斯的粉丝，我常常想他本可以多做多少事，但在那个时代，你一次只能做一件事，没有人拥有超级投票权之类的。然后谷歌出现了，扎克伯格出现了，就切换到了创始人控制公司的时代。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: and they could be much more aggressive with the business plan and that works really well here in the valley.
turns.zh: 他们可以在商业计划上更加激进，这在硅谷非常有效。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But then Elon came along and reinvented it again where you can do multiple things at the same time. So, this is working out incredibly well for Figure and Harken. If you just said Harken 9 months from today could be bigger than Figure, it was just a mind-blowing statement.
turns.zh: 但后来埃隆出现了，再次重新发明了它，你可以同时做多件事。所以，这对 Figure 和 Harken 来说非常成功。如果你说 Harken 在 9 个月后可能比 Figure 更大，那只是一个令人震惊的声明。

turns.en: You said 3 months from today.
turns.zh: 你说的是 3 个月后。

turns.en: 3 months from today.
turns.zh: 3 个月后。

turns.en: I mean like Harken's just going like this, guys. Like I just like it's it is going really well. Like so, we'll see. I was just making sure.
turns.zh: 我是说 Harken 就像这样发展，伙计们。就像，它进展得真的很好。所以，我们拭目以待。我只是确认一下。

turns.en: Got this other thing about school safety, you know, that is yeah, which is, you know, not going to be bigger than the other two companies, but it's important for the world happening concurrent. Like the power of an entrepreneur today is so much bigger than it was in the Steve Jobs era, let alone the Zuckerberg era. So, I think it's really inspiring. Do you think a 20-year-old entrepreneur today can walk in your footsteps or is AI going to make it all too late and it's, you know, the ship has sailed?
turns.zh: 还有关于学校安全的另一件事，你知道，那不会比另外两家公司更大，但它对世界很重要，同时进行。如今企业家的力量比史蒂夫·乔布斯时代大得多，更不用说扎克伯格时代了。所以，我觉得这真的很鼓舞人心。你认为今天 20 岁的企业家能追随你的脚步吗？还是 AI 会让一切为时已晚，机会已经错过了？

turns.en: Yeah, I mean I think one thing I'll say is I'm like completely dying. Like three kids, like three companies, like I'm just like I've been here every night for whole year. I'm just like man has it been hard. But it's like you know it's the best time of my life and I never want to do it again you know. It's like it's been going great. Yeah listen I like the future generation is going to be great. Everything's going to be AI native. You'll be able to build any type of hardware just through talking and robots like it's going to be so cool. Like really where the AI is really missing is like it has like no imagination today. And we're going to be bound by this imagination and it's like this is what entrepreneurs do best right? Like you always have like a little notepad I always still do say have a notepad of like all the business ideas like I can think of and just I still keep them to this day and just like it's a you know they're great at idea generation great about thinking about the future like this is going to be an unbounded opportunity for every like new entrepreneur like behind me growing up and it just maybe one of the it'll be the it'll mark the best time in the world for entrepreneurs in history and now you have an ecosystem here like today that like for entrepreneurship like and when I was graduating school like it wasn't like it wasn't conceivable you'd start as an entrepreneur like it was just like you don't do nobody does that like so I had a job for a few years before I started it. I wish I started even sooner starting companies so but like you know now you can go do that you can get capital for it there's incubators there's people want to work at the startups it's fun like you have this whole like community built around it too which is just like going to propel these future entrepreneurs further.
turns.zh: 是的，我的意思是，我想说的一件事是我快累死了。三个孩子，三家公司，我整年每晚都在这里。天啊，这太难了。但你知道，这是我一生中最美好的时光，我再也不想重来一次了。一切进展顺利。听着，未来一代会很棒。一切都会是 AI 原生的。你可以通过说话来构建任何类型的硬件，机器人，那会很酷。AI 真正缺失的地方是它今天没有想象力。我们将受限于这种想象力，而这正是企业家最擅长的，对吧？你总是有一个小记事本，我一直都这样，有一个记事本记录我能想到的所有商业想法，我至今还保留着。他们擅长产生想法，擅长思考未来，这对每个新企业家来说将是一个无限的机会，就像我成长过程中一样，这可能是历史上对企业家来说最好的时代。现在你在这里有一个生态系统，就像今天对于创业来说，当我毕业时，你不可能想到你会成为企业家，就像没人这样做。所以我开始创业前做了几年工作。我希望能更早开始创业，但现在你可以去做，你可以获得资本，有孵化器，有人想在初创公司工作，这很有趣，你有一个完整的社区围绕它，这将推动这些未来的企业家走得更远。

turns.en: I like to joke we've all been promised a three and four day work week we've invented a 10-day work week.
turns.zh: 我喜欢开玩笑说，我们都被承诺过每周三到四天工作制，但我们发明了每周 10 天工作制。

turns.en: I mean I like working man. Let's just call what it is. It's just like I like grinding it out and working this. I think everybody here with me likes it too. We just like we have a bunch of groups that like to work hard and we've made it this like dirty word out here in the valley and so like you know like a lot of folks coming here and be like you guys are like the most unsilicon valley company I've ever seen. Like we work hard. We come in on the weekends like we work nights like we just we just it and there's not enough of that anymore, you know? It's just like almost like we interview people like, oh, what's your like day off strategy and like work from home? Like we don't have any of that. You come in here every day and you like work with us and we're going to work with you. Like, you know, my Baki guys can't work from home. They got to be in the line every day.
turns.zh: 我是说，我喜欢工作，伙计。我们就实话实说吧。我就是喜欢埋头苦干，努力工作。我觉得这里的每个人都喜欢。我们有一群喜欢努力工作的人，而在硅谷，我们把努力工作变成了一个肮脏的词。所以，很多人来这里会说，你们是我见过的最不像硅谷的公司。我们努力工作，周末来，晚上工作，我们就是这样，现在这种精神不够多了，你知道吗？几乎就像我们面试别人时会问，哦，你的休息日策略是什么？在家工作？我们没有这些。你每天来这里和我们一起工作，我们也会和你一起工作。就像我的 Baki 伙计们不能在家工作，他们每天都要在线。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And same with us. We got to get in line too. So like anyway, it's just um
turns.zh: 我们也一样。我们也得在线。所以，不管怎样，只是……

turns.en: What you're building is so much cooler than virtually any day job, you know? I mean, it's got to be even if you're working twice as hard, it's got to be so much rewarding at the end more rewarding at the end of the day to look at what you physically built. That's just Also, I didn't anticipate how much the office environment is elevated by the walking around robots.
turns.zh: 你所建造的东西几乎比任何日常工作都酷得多，你知道吗？我的意思是，即使你工作加倍努力，最终也会更有回报，一天结束时看着你亲手建造的东西会更 rewarding。还有，我没想到办公室环境会因为走来走去的机器人而提升这么多。

turns.en: Better.
turns.zh: 更好。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It's bizarre. It's like it just adds energy to the building somehow.
turns.zh: 这很奇怪。就好像它以某种方式给大楼增添了能量。

turns.zh: 所以一年后，我们会回来做我们的 Figure 4 回顾。

turns.zh: 你回来，Figure 4，Figure 4，帮你安排好，登记，给你水、咖啡，带你转转，给你参观，然后我们采访见。

turns.en: And we'll include Figure Four in the interview too.
turns.zh: 我们也会在采访中包括 Figure 4。

turns.en: Just like honestly Figure Four can speak on my behalf.
turns.zh: 老实说，Figure 4 可以代表我发言。

turns.en: That's so fun.
turns.zh: 那太有趣了。

turns.en: It's like you know what I mean?
turns.zh: 就像你明白我的意思吗？

turns.en: Uh but thank you so much.
turns.zh: 呃，但非常感谢你。

turns.en: for having me.
turns.zh: 邀请我。

turns.zh: 是的。现在当我们停止拍摄时，我们会去看你在 Figure 4 中的秘密设备。

turns.en: Yeah, perfect.
turns.zh: 是的，完美。

turns.zh: 成交。
